title: The daily commute
paragraphs: The daily journey from home to work is one of those things many of us have to endure. Whether it's by train, on a bus, on a bike or on foot, it's a chore that some would rather do without, but it's part of the daily grind if we have to work!

We all have stories of commuting nightmares - a tube train stuck in a tunnel or a bus journey where people are packed in like sardines. In London, where there is an extensive transport network, complaining about delays, cancellations and the price of their season ticket, has become a commuter's favourite pastime but their problems are relatively minor compared to ones that travellers in other parts of the world face. In Nairobi, for example, commuters have to keep windows shut to avoid someone stealing their belongings.

It's no surprise that the daily commute is stressful and according to research, women are more likely to experience stress during their journey than men. This is because they're more likely to do something which is being called 'trip chaining' - where they make one or more stops on the way to work or when going home - for example to drop off or pick up the kids from school - and this makes it more likely that something will go wrong with their journey.

The stress of commuting can be bad for your health too especially if you travel longer distances. According to Christine Hoehner, researcher at Washington University School of Medicine, "adults who commuted longer distances from home to work were less physically active, less physically fit, weighed more and had higher blood pressure than those people who had shorter commutes."

But this American researcher must be talking about people who don't do active travel because if you commute a long distance by bike you are likely to be more active. However, there is the risk of being knocked off your bike and feeling embarrassed about wearing Lycra! How's your journey to work, school or college?

vocabulary.entry: chore [n.] /tʃɔː/ 日常琐事；令人厌烦的任务
vocabulary.example: Doing the laundry is such a chore.
vocabulary.translation: 洗衣服真是件烦人的事。

vocabulary.entry: daily grind [n.] /ˈdeɪli ɡraɪnd/ 日常枯燥的工作；日常奔波 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: After ten years of the daily grind, he decided to quit his job and travel.
vocabulary.translation: 经过十年的日常奔波，他决定辞职去旅行。

vocabulary.entry: commuting nightmares [n. pl.] /kəˈmjuːtɪŋ ˈnaɪtmeəz/ 通勤噩梦 (单数: commuting nightmare；口语)
vocabulary.example: Strikes and signal failures are typical commuting nightmares.
vocabulary.translation: 罢工和信号故障是典型的通勤噩梦。

vocabulary.entry: packed in like sardines [phr.] /pækt ɪn laɪk sɑːˈdiːnz/ 像沙丁鱼一样挤在一起 (口语；明喻)
vocabulary.example: The train was so crowded that we were packed in like sardines.
vocabulary.translation: 火车太挤了，我们像沙丁鱼一样挤在一起。

vocabulary.entry: extensive transport network [n.] /ɪkˈstensɪv ˈtrænspɔːt ˈnetwɜːk/ 广泛的交通网络 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: London has an extensive transport network including buses, tubes and trains.
vocabulary.translation: 伦敦拥有包括公交车、地铁和火车在内的广泛交通网络。

vocabulary.entry: season ticket [n.] /ˈsiːzən ˈtɪkɪt/ 季票；定期票
vocabulary.example: A season ticket is cheaper than buying daily tickets.
Gardening is a popular pastime among the elderly.
vocabulary.translation: 园艺是老年人中流行的消遣。

vocabulary.entry: trip chaining [n.] /trɪp ˈtʃeɪnɪŋ/ 行程链 (专业词汇；交通规划术语)
vocabulary.example: Trip chaining is common among parents who drop off children on their way to work.
vocabulary.translation: 行程链在上班途中送孩子的父母中很常见。

vocabulary.example: Moving house is one of the most stressful things you can do.
vocabulary.translation: 搬家是你能做的最有压力的事情之一。

vocabulary.entry: physically active [phr.] /ˈfɪzɪkəli ˈæktɪv/ 身体活跃的 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Children should be physically active for at least an hour every day.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们每天应该至少进行一小时的体育活动。

vocabulary.entry: blood pressure [n.] /blʌd ˈpreʃə/ 血压 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: High blood pressure increases the risk of heart disease.
vocabulary.translation: 高血压会增加心脏病的风险。

vocabulary.entry: active travel [n.] /ˈæktɪv ˈtrævəl/ 主动通勤；绿色出行 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Cycling and walking are forms of active travel.
vocabulary.translation: 骑自行车和步行是主动通勤的形式。

vocabulary.entry: knocked off your bike [phr.] /nɒkt ɒf jɔː baɪk/ 从自行车上被撞倒 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: She was knocked off her bike by a car turning left.
vocabulary.translation: 她被一辆左转的汽车从自行车上撞倒。

vocabulary.entry: belongings [n. pl.] /bɪˈlɒŋɪŋz/ 财物；行李 (单数: belonging)
vocabulary.example: Please do not leave your belongings unattended.
vocabulary.translation: 请不要让你的财物无人看管。

vocabulary.example: She commutes from Oxford to London every day.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天从牛津通勤到伦敦。

vocabulary.example: Researchers have discovered a new species of frog.
vocabulary.translation: 研究人员发现了一种新的青蛙物种。

vocabulary.entry: physically fit [phr.] /ˈfɪzɪkəli fɪt/ 体能好的；身体健康的
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise helps you stay physically fit.
vocabulary.translation: 定期锻炼有助于保持身体健康。

vocabulary.example: The baby weighed three kilograms at birth.
vocabulary.translation: 这个婴儿出生时体重三公斤。

sentences.english: The daily journey from home to work is one of those things many of us have to endure.
sentences.chinese: 每天往返于家和工作的旅程是我们许多人不得不忍受的事情之一。

sentences.english: Whether it's by train, on a bus, on a bike or on foot, it's a chore that some would rather do without, but it's part of the daily grind if we have to work!
sentences.chinese: 无论是乘火车、搭公交车、骑自行车还是步行，这是一种有些人宁愿没有的例行琐事，但如果我们必须工作，这种重复枯燥的日常琐事就是工作的一部分！

sentences.english: We all have stories of commuting nightmares - a tube train stuck in a tunnel or a bus journey where people are packed in like sardines.
sentences.chinese: 我们都有关于通勤噩梦的故事——地铁列车堵在隧道里，或者公交车上的乘客像沙丁鱼一样挤在一起。

sentences.english: In London, where there is an extensive transport network, complaining about delays, cancellations and the price of their season ticket, has become a commuter's favourite pastime but their problems are relatively minor compared to ones that travellers in other parts of the world face.
sentences.chinese: 在拥有密集交通网络的伦敦，抱怨延误、取消和季票价格已成为通勤者最喜欢的消遣，但与其他地区旅行者面临的问题相比，他们的问题相对较小。

sentences.english: In Nairobi, for example, commuters have to keep windows shut to avoid someone stealing their belongings.
sentences.chinese: 例如，在内罗毕，通勤者必须关上车窗，以防有人偷走他们的财物。

sentences.english: It's no surprise that the daily commute is stressful and according to research, women are more likely to experience stress during their journey than men.
sentences.chinese: 日常通勤压力大并不奇怪，根据研究，女性在通勤过程中比男性更容易感到压力。

sentences.english: This is because they're more likely to do something which is being called 'trip chaining' - where they make one or more stops on the way to work or when going home - for example to drop off or pick up the kids from school - and this makes it more likely that something will go wrong with their journey.
sentences.chinese: 这是因为她们更有可能进行所谓的“行程链”——在上班或回家的路上进行一次或多次停留——例如送孩子上学或接孩子放学——这增加了她们旅程中出现问题的可能性。

sentences.english: The stress of commuting can be bad for your health too especially if you travel longer distances.
sentences.chinese: 通勤的压力也可能对健康有害，尤其是如果你通勤距离较长。

sentences.english: According to Christine Hoehner, researcher at Washington University School of Medicine, "adults who commuted longer distances from home to work were less physically active, less physically fit, weighed more and had higher blood pressure than those people who had shorter commutes."
sentences.chinese: 根据华盛顿大学医学院的研究员克里斯汀·霍纳的说法，“与通勤距离较短的人相比，从家到工作地点通勤距离较长的成年人身体活动较少，体能较差，体重更重，血压更高。”

sentences.english: But this American researcher must be talking about people who don't do active travel because if you commute a long distance by bike you are likely to be more active.
sentences.chinese: 但这位美国研究员一定是在谈论那些不进行主动通勤的人，因为如果你骑自行车通勤较长距离，你可能会更活跃。

sentences.english: However, there is the risk of being knocked off your bike and feeling embarrassed about wearing Lycra!
sentences.chinese: 然而，骑自行车有被撞倒的风险，而且穿着莱卡材质的衣服可能会让人感到尴尬！

sentences.english: How's your journey to work, school or college?
sentences.chinese: 你上班、上学或去学校的旅程是怎样的呢？
